title: xAI ships Grok 4.7 with 2.1T parameters and SpaceX-sourced training data
subtitle: The model lands in GitHub Copilot and Cursor at the same price as Grok 4.6 after Musk walked back the timeline five times over two months.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: xAI released Grok 4.7 on Monday, September 21, describing it as a notable improvement over Grok 4.6 at the same price and speed. The model carries 2.1 trillion parameters — a 40% jump from Grok 4.6's 1.5 trillion — priced at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens. It began rolling out the same day to GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Grok Build, the Grok API, and third-party coding harnesses.

The pitch is longer horizons on hard problems and stronger self-checking, aimed squarely at agentic coding workflows. xAI folded in supplemental training data pulled from SpaceX — Starlink satellite telemetry, manufacturing records, and engineering failure logs — arguing the model reasons better about hardware and physical systems than models trained purely on internet text. The company also says the release carries its strongest safety guardrails to date, though it published no evaluation numbers alongside that claim.

The release arrived after a string of missed dates. Musk pushed the timeline back at least five times since late July, from "four weeks out" to "a few weeks" to "3 to 4 weeks" to "10 days" on September 1, then "needs a few more days to cook" on September 11. That pattern matters because it fits a broader shift: frontier labs are shipping incremental point releases rather than the step changes that defined 2023 through 2025, and the delays now come from tuning rather than pretraining.

A note for learners: when a lab folds proprietary operational data into training — telemetry, failure logs, internal specs — the model's edge is data provenance, not a new architecture. If you're evaluating Grok 4.7 for a task, test it on questions that would exercise the SpaceX data (physical systems, hardware failure modes, control loops) rather than the general benchmarks that competing models are already tuned for.
